jobs.location: New York, NY - Hybrid; San Francisco, CA - Hybrid
jobs.description:
About Gusto

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About the Role:

Gusto offers payroll processing for hundreds of thousands of businesses and their employees, and that activity is supervised by state money transmission regulators across the country. Our financial services licenses are foundational to how Gusto operates, and keeping that portfolio current, accurate, and examination-ready is mission critical.

Gusto is looking for a hands-on regulatory compliance professional to own the day-to-day management of Gusto's licensing portfolio. You will run the licensing lifecycle end to end across NMLS and non-NMLS states: applications, renewals, amendments, change notices, periodic reporting, surety bonds, and ongoing license conditions. You will also serve as a core contributor in state examinations, managing request lists, evidence, and commitments This is an individual contributor role reporting to the Head of Financial Services. At Gusto, Legal & Compliance operates as an AI-native team. You will use and help improve AI-enabled licensing workflows, including our licensing and examination registries, filing calendars, and regulatory change tracking, with appropriate human-in-the-loop controls for accuracy and accountability.

About the Team:

Gusto’s Legal & Compliance team partners closely with product and engineering teams to enable innovation, facilitate responsible company growth, accelerate Gusto’s roadmap, and deliver compliant products to our customers.

We are passionate about applying AI-native ways of working, thoughtful compliance risk management, and a daily service mindset to improve the experience of small business owners and their employees. Each team member is an owner, a trusted advisor, and a meaningful contributor to Gusto’s mission.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

- Own day-to-day management of Gusto's money transmitter (MTL) and related state financial services licenses, maintaining a current system of record for every license, condition, and deadline.

- Manage Gusto's NMLS company record end to end (MU1, MU2, MU3 filings, amendments, and disclosure updates), and run the annual NMLS and state renewal cycles.

- Prepare and file new license applications, expansion filings, and change notices or amendments, partnering with counsel and managing regulator approvals for changes in control, officers, or business activities.

- Own the quarterly NMLS MSB Call Report and state periodic, annual, and transaction volume reports, coordinating with Finance and Treasury on financial statement, net worth, and investment reporting.

- Manage the surety bond portfolio and the regulatory filing calendar, ensuring on-time filings with documented evidence for examination.

- Serve as a key contributor on state and multi-state examinations, managing request lists, evidence collection, document production, and quality control.

- Support examination findings and license conditions through to closure, coordinate high-risk data requests, and manage regulator correspondence, escalating substantive matters.

- Monitor state money transmission developments (MTMA adoption, NMLS/CSBS and rule changes) and assess their impact on Gusto's licenses and filings.

- Translate licensing requirements into clear procedures, checklists, and guidance for cross-functional partners.

- Use AI-enabled tools to automate filing prep, deadline tracking, and evidence assembly with documented human review, and identify gaps to make the program more scalable and examination-ready.

Here’s what we're looking for:

- 5+ years of experience in regulatory compliance, licensing, or regulatory operations at a fintech, payments company, money services business, or regulated financial institution, including at least 3 years managing money transmission licenses; experience with additional state license types (lending, servicing, collections, PEO) or at a high-growth fintech operating through sponsor bank or embedded finance partnerships is a plus.

- Experience with PEO licensing is a plus, particularly for candidates who have operated across both MTL and PEO licensing regimes.

- Paralegal background preferred, especially with experience on regulatory filings, licensing documentation, or change of control notices.

- Hands-on NMLS expertise, including MU1, MU2, and MU3 filings, the annual renewal cycle, the MSB Call Report, and Electronic Surety Bonds.

- Working knowledge of state money transmission requirements, including net worth, permissible investments, surety bonds, change of control, authorized delegates, and periodic reporting.

- Direct experience supporting state or multistate regulatory examinations, including request list management, evidence assembly, and findings remediation; familiarity with CSBS multi-state examination frameworks like One Company One Exam and MMET is a plus.

- Rigorous documentation discipline: every filing accurate, every deadline tracked, every submission retained. A Notary Public commission, or willingness to obtain one, is a plus.

- Strong organizational and project management skills, with the ability to manage high-volume, deadline-driven work across many jurisdictions at once; experience with compliance workflow, GRC, or licensing management platforms is a plus.

- Clear written and verbal communication, with the ability to coordinate inputs across Finance, Legal, Product, and Operations.

- Sound judgment on when to resolve an issue independently and when to escalate to leadership or counsel.

- Demonstrated experience using AI tools (Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini, Glean, Notion AI, or similar) to improve compliance or licensing workflows, paired with the discipline to review AI output before relying on it.

Our cash compensation amount for this role is $110,640/yr to $136,456/yr in Denver & most major metro locations, and $133,615/yr to $164,792/yr for San Francisco & New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors including candidate location, experience and expertise and may vary from the amounts listed above.

At Gusto, we don't use titles the traditional way, as a signal of rank or hierarchy. Instead, our titles describe two things at once — your craft (what you do, e.g. Engineering, Design) and your scope of ownership (what you're accountable for) — which is why you'll see something like "Head of X" instead of a rank word like "Director" that tells you neither. Because of this, the title on this posting may look different from what you'd expect based on the scope and seniority of the role, and from how similar roles are typically titled elsewhere. If you have questions about how this role compares to your current title or level, your recruiter can help translate.

Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale.

Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas.

When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

Reliable, consistent presence: We expect regular and predictable attendance, whether you're working in-office, hybrid, or fully remote, so that you stay closely connected to your team, customers, and stakeholders in real time and ensure colleagues and customers receive the timely support and responsiveness they deserve.

Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto.

About the Role:

Payments at Gusto aren't just infrastructure, they're the reason people get paid on time, every time. Payment Operations sits within Gusto's Money team, a cross-functional group spanning Engineering, Product, and Operations that powers money movement across Gusto's growing product surface: core payroll, contractor payments, international money movement, and new business offerings like PEO.

As the Payment Operations Manager, you'll lead a team of Payment Operations Analysts and own the health of Gusto's payment operations end to end: the ACH, wire, RTP, and international contractor payment rails, the day-to-day operations behind our bank and payment partner relationships, and the operational side of the compliance programs that keep all of it running within regulatory bounds. You'll work closely with Engineering, Product, Accounting, Risk, Legal, and CX to get there.

This is a role for someone who can zoom in and personally work a ticket or partner escalation, and zoom out to manage the team and keep a compliance program on track, in the same afternoon. You build strong people, hold partners accountable, and bring rigor to how the team operates.

Here’s what you’ll do day-to-day:

Lead and grow the team

- Manage a team of Payment Operations Analysts. Hire, coach, and develop them, set clear expectations, and give direct feedback. Own team-level SLAs, on-call rotation and escalation paths, and reporting, and use data to spot where the team's processes are breaking down and fix the root cause, not just the symptom. You're accountable for the team's output and for the growth of the people on it.

Manage day-to-day bank and payment partner operations

- Own the operational relationship with our banking and payment partners, including issue triage, escalations, and operational reviews, and personally work individual tickets yourself when the queue backs up or SLAs are at risk. Partner closely with the team that owns the strategic partnership on renewals and due diligence.

Operate the compliance programs that keep payments running

- Execute the day-to-day work behind Gusto's Nacha, unclaimed property, and bank compliance programs, and Payment Ops' portion of SOC 1 audits. Financial Services Compliance and Payroll Compliance own these programs; you're the operational partner who keeps documentation, controls, and evidence current and coordinates with them and GRC when new requirements land.

Drive incident response for payment operations

- When something breaks at scale, whether it's a failed batch, a reconciliation break, or a payment partner outage, you're in the investigation yourself, not just directing it. You keep stakeholders informed and drive the retro that prevents it from happening again.

Partner with Product and Engineering

- Bring the team's operational insight into product and engineering conversations. Flag risk early, weigh in on payment-related specs, and make sure operational needs are represented, without owning the product roadmap yourself.

Lead with AI

- Model and encourage the use of AI across the team, whether that's faster investigation, cleaner documentation, or automating repetitive work.

- 7+ years of hands-on experience in payment operations, banking operations, or treasury operations, including direct ownership of escalations, partner issues, or ticket queues, and 2+ years directly managing a team

- Deep working knowledge of domestic payment rails (ACH/Nacha, wires, RTP) and experience with international money movement is a strong plus

- Experience managing the operational side of a bank or payment partner relationship, including escalations, issue triage, and partner reviews

- Track record of operating within a compliance program (Nacha Risk Self-Assessment, SOC 1, unclaimed property, or similar), including audits and controls work

- Strong people leadership: you've hired, coached, and managed performance for a team of analysts or similar operational ICs

- Comfortable operating with real ambiguity and driving cross-functional work without needing a fully defined process

- AI-fluent: you use it as a genuine lever for yourself and expect your team to as well

- Nacha AAP or AFPP certification is a strong plus

At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

About Design at Gusto

Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference. We believe great design can make hard things possible, even delightful.

We are building an AI-native creative organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for people who are already working this way: using AI to keep a growing team's systems, schedules, and stakeholders aligned, not just to move faster. This isn't a future aspiration — it's how we work now, and it's changing what creative operations looks like at Gusto and across the industry.

About the Opportunity

Gusto's Brand Studio is at an exciting inflection point. We’re scaling the team and building the systems to meet our growing ambition, from the brand refresh to increasingly complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns.

We're looking for a Senior Creative Program Manager to be the connective tissue between Brand Studio and the cross-functional partners we build with: Marketing, PMM, R&D, and Legal. This role reports to the Manager of Creative Operations, who sets the operational roadmap and defines how the creative team interfaces with Marketing. You'll independently execute against that roadmap: unblocking projects, managing cross-functional stakeholders, and driving timelines across standard tier-1/tier-2 launches and complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns, each with its own approval checkpoint and parallel workstream.

A core part of the role is helping stand up, optimize, and maintain the team's project infrastructure  including the Brand Studio dashboard (an all-up project view for resourcing and capacity planning) and its task tracker, and driving consistent adoption and project management hygiene across the team and stakeholders. The Manager of Creative Operations leads the systems-level architecture; you'll help build it out and own ongoing optimization and maintenance.

If you bring calm and clarity to fast-changing, multi-stakeholder work and you want to help shape, scale, and optimize the processes that let a growing in-house creative team meet this moment, this is your role.

Here's what you'll do day-to-day

- Serve as the primary point of contact for cross-functional stakeholders (Marketing, PMM, Legal, R&D) across active projects including running daily/weekly updates, unblocking work, and escalating when needed

- Build and maintain creative workback schedules, keeping the project source of truth (in partnership with Marketing) current as scope, deliverables, and deadlines shift

- Manage vendor and agency relationships end to end including contractor paperwork, PO management, onboarding/access, and day-to-day production coordination with partners like STATE, Superside, and Uprise Art

- Own the legal & compliance review pipeline for your projects including submitting requests, chasing disclosures and input, and keeping creative moving through legal feedback

- Flag risks and dependencies early across creative projects, escalating to leadership before they become delivery problems

- Schedule and run feedback checkpoints from internal crits and stakeholder reviews to leadership sign-offs, and consolidate feedback back to the team

- Coordinate production logistics for shoots, agency staffing, on-site support, and the stakeholder management that comes with it

- Help stand up, optimize, and maintain the team's AI-enabled project infrastructure, including the Brand Studio dashboard and task tracker, and keep project management hygiene consistent across the team

- Run retros and drive process improvements for better templates, tighter rituals, small workflow automations

Here's what we're looking for

- 5–7 years of experience in creative, marketing, or brand production/project management — in-house or a blend of in-house and agency-side — with hands-on experience running point on multiple active projects, stakeholders, and vendors at once

- Experience managing complex, multi-channel integrated campaigns with multiple channel owners,  including multiple approval checkpoints and parallel workstreams within a single project,  and balancing a portfolio of several such projects simultaneously

- Experience building and maintaining workback schedules and/or project hubs (expertise doing this in Notion a plus) that a team relies on, and helping stand up, optimize, or drive adoption of project management infrastructure such as dashboards, task trackers, or similar systems across a team

- Familiarity optimizing and maintaining AI-enabled tools and designing systems from scratch when needed; hands-on, daily use of AI tools for drafting, synthesis, and status updates

- Comfort operating in ambiguity and shifting scope and experience in an agile, fast-changing environment (integrated campaigns, product marketing, or paid media).

- Strong written and verbal communication; interest in running retros and improving process (templates, rituals, small workflow automations)

- You bring order and calm to complexity. For example, a project without a clear owner, timeline, or next step doesn't sit well with you.
